learning_objective: 🎯 Dive into the service sector! Learn about the jobs that focus on providing services, knowledge, and high-level decision-making rather than physical goods.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: These involve providing services rather than producing tangible goods. This includes trade, transport, communication, teaching, healthcare, and retail.

Tourism is the world's largest tertiary activity. Medical tourism occurs when people travel to other countries specifically for medical treatment (like traveling to India for high-quality, affordable surgeries).

The 'Knowledge Sector'. These are specialized tertiary activities focused on information generation, collection, production, and dissemination (e.g., software developers, researchers, financial analysts).
The highest level of decision-making and policy creation. This includes top government officials, corporate CEOs, and senior research scientists. They represent the 'gold collar' professions.

Giving work to an outside agency to improve efficiency and reduce costs. Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) handles customer service, while Knowledge Process Outsourcing (KPO) involves highly skilled research tasks.

fun_activity.title: 👔 Collar Color Check
fun_activity.instructions: Classify the jobs in your family! Red collar = Primary (farmer), Blue collar = Secondary (factory worker), Pink/White collar = Tertiary/Quaternary (teacher/software engineer), Gold collar = Quinary (CEO/Minister).

exam_tips: 📌 Distinguish strictly between Quaternary (knowledge/information) and Quinary (high-level decisions/policy making).
📌 Understand why companies outsource: primarily for cost reduction and efficiency by utilizing cheaper labor in developing nations.
📌 Medical tourism is a highly probable short-answer topic. Know examples of countries that benefit from it (India, Thailand, Singapore).
quick_recap: ⭐ The service sector is the largest contributor to employment and GDP in developed countries.
⭐ Outsourcing often results in a shift of jobs from developed to developing countries.
⭐ Quaternary and quinary activities are essentially advanced sub-categories of the tertiary sector.
